title: The Distinction Between Primary and Secondary Groups
text: Sociology distinguishes between primary and secondary group interactions, recognizing that these structures fundamentally shape individual identities. Primary groups are defined by intimate, face-to-face association and enduring emotional ties (such as immediate family or childhood friendships), which provide the basis for initial socialization. Secondary groups, however, are larger, more impersonal units formed to achieve specific, instrumental goals—examples include classrooms or professional workplaces. The shift in role expectation between these two group types is a cornerstone of understanding how an individual’s self-concept evolves throughout different life stages.
